rows.summary: This journal entry initiates the research project 'record_robustness' to investigate the mechanisms enabling consistent records across independent observers. By mapping the theoretical foundations of quantum Darwinism, spectrum broadcast structures, and strong quantum Darwinism, we aim to operationalize the conditions under which environment-induced redundancy establishes public reliability. The initial phase focuses on extracting metrics for observer agreement from current literature, specifically evaluating whether redundant information in the environment is sufficient for robust record formation or if additional stability criteria are required. We maintain focus on distinguishing consensus from causal influence and identifying counterexamples where apparent observer agreement may fail.
rows.title: Establishing Operational Metrics for Observer Agreement in Quantum Records
